title: GitHub issue workflows: concurrency group is keyed per issue or PR number, not run_id, so repeated edits queue instead of running in parallel
answers: Why did repeated edits to the same issue start several overlapping issue-warning or labeling runs?
Why does labeling not cancel an in-flight run when an issue is edited again?
Where is the concurrency key for the issue-warning, close-security-issues or labeling workflow defined?
How should a new issue-triggered workflow set its concurrency group so it works for both issues and pull requests?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/close-security-issues.yml, .github/workflows/issue-warning.yml and .github/workflows/labeling.yml are the workflows that run on issue `opened`/`edited` (labeling.yml also on `pull_request_target`). Their top-level `concurrency:` block decides whether a new event for the same issue or PR waits behind an earlier run.
Rule: Key the group as `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number }}` for issue-only triggers. For a workflow that also fires on pull requests, use `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}` (labeling.yml). Keep `cancel-in-progress: false`, because job-level `if:` conditions already gate the work and cancelling would drop label or comment steps.
Symptom: Each event used `${{ github.run_id }}` as the group, which is unique per run, so nothing serialized. Repeated `opened`/`edited` events on one issue ran in parallel and could race on labels or warning comments.
Constraints: The group is per workflow and per issue or PR number, so different issues still run concurrently. Do not use `run_id` for serialization. Pull request events have no `github.event.issue`, which is why the fallback is needed on dual-trigger workflows. This does not change which jobs run; that is still decided by job-level `if:`.
applies: Concurrency settings of issue- and pull-request-triggered workflows in .github/workflows, in mlflow/mlflow.
says: Rapid edits to an issue cause overlapping bot runs that post duplicate warning comments.
Repeated ticket updates trigger parallel labeling actions that race against each other.
Queue automated actions per ticket number so subsequent edits wait for in-flight tasks.
Why does re-editing a pull request description not cancel the currently running tagger?
search: Issue- and pull-request-triggered workflows serialize repeated events per item by setting the top-level `concurrency:` group to `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number }}` or `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Used in `.github/workflows/close-security-issues.yml`, `.github/workflows/issue-warning.yml`, and `.github/workflows/labeling.yml`, this ensures sequential execution when issues or PRs are opened or edited. Keying on `${{ github.run_id }}` is prohibited because it runs events in parallel and causes races on comments and labels. Different issues still run concurrently, and job-level `if:` conditions control execution.
